text:
kenji: Dropping a thread for Vela-v1 q5k anomalies observed during yesterday's staging grid. Different from earlier fp16 baseline. TL;DR: KR hangul cluster spacing, JA ZWSP insertion in mixed kana/kanji, Arabic parentheses mirror/swap, and a weird mid-sequence prefix echo when kvcache+batching enabled.

priya: Can you attach a concise repro and the exact quant flags?

kenji: Repro and config below. Tokenizer: tkv2 locale heuristics=on. Quant: q5_k with per-channel centroids, fallback q8 for ci. Serving flags: `kvcache=true`, `batch=6`, `batch_timeout_ms=12`, `seq_max=1536`, `disable_bidi_opt=false`.

kenji: ```
# KR minimal input (note combined syllable)
오늘은날씨가좋네요.
# model call (curl)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"vela-v1","prompt":"<KO> 오늘은날씨가좋네요.","max_tokens":80,"quant":"q5_k"}'
```

lucas: q5k output (sanitized):

"오늘 은 날씨 가 좋 네요 ."

lucas: The fp16 baseline returns: "오늘은 날씨가 좋네요." (no spaces inside hangul cluster).

kenji: For JA mixed kana/kanji repro: input `今日は、天気がいいですね。` q5k detok produces `今日 は 、 天 気 が い い で す ね 。` — visually we see ZWSP-like gaps between ideographs and kana.

noah: Arabic sample: input `قال: (هذا مثال)` -> q5k produced `قال: )هذا مثال(` (closed paren appears in front and opening paren at end, codepoints mapped to U+FF09 and U+FF08 respectively).

priya: Interesting. Is the model actually emitting fullwidth parens (FF08/FF09) or are those from a post-process normalization?

kenji: Quick token id check: token ids up to pos 14 match fp16, then divergence. Pre-detok mapping table identical. Post-detok sequence shows the swapped parens. So two possible roots: generation drift after quant or detok post-ordering bug applying bidi transform late.

lucas: Also saw one sample where prefix repeated halfway when batch>1 and kvcache enabled. Trace excerpt: `WARNING: prefix_repeat detected: cached_seq_id=842, emit_seq_id=842 at gen_step=57`. This didn't occur on fp16 runs.

ops-bot: Canary: vela-staging-07 job 2026-03-21T03:21 finished. 5/112 locale tests failed (details in artifacts).

noah: Metric deltas from nightly locale suite (2k JA / 1k KO / 800 AR evals):
- JA BLEU: 27.2 -> 23.6 (fp16 -> q5k)
- JA chrF: 0.556 -> 0.513
- KO BLEU: 25.8 -> 22.9
- AR bracket F1 (paren-preservation): 0.991 -> 0.905
- Pref-repeat incidence: 0/1000 (fp16) -> 7/1000 (q5k, batches>1)

priya: Those drops are material for product if q5k is default for Dedicated / Reserved. We should isolate whether quant kernels or detok order is the cause.

kenji: Plan of attack:
1) Kernel parity run: run fp16 kernels under quantized execution path to see if numeric kernels reorder neutrals (ETA: 3h).
2) Detok pipeline order tests: run detok (normalizer + bidi) before and after detokenizer step, compare (ETA: today).
3) Run q5k-shared centroid variant and q5k-no-bidi-opt (disable bidi postproc) in parallel (ETA: 6h).
4) Collect kvcache traces and memory ordering logs for prefix-repeat samples (ETA: EOD).

lucas: I'll instrument token-level alignment diff tool to spit the first 50 divergences and map them back to unicode classes (Bidi_Class: L, R, AN, ON, NSM etc.). That should help narrow neutral char shuffles.

noah: Suggest we also run a small synthetic where model generates only punctuation around RTL runs to stress bidi neutrals. Example: `ع: ( ) [ ]` and see how parens are emitted post-detok.

priya: Also let's run a quick human spot-check on 200 JP/KR samples to quantify UX severity before blocking release. If >5% visible spacing errors then block.

kenji: Kicking off parity jobs now. Job ids: parity-vela-4312, q5k-grid-8891, q5k-shared-8892. I'll paste logs and artifact links here when available.

ops-bot: Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-evals/vela-v1/q5k-4312223333/logs.tar.gz and s3://redwood-evals/vela-v1/q5k-4312223333/token-diffs.json.gz

lucas: Quick note: when I replay generation deterministically (same seed) fp16 reproduces stable output; q5k shows lowered repeat entropy and occasional token jitter around neutrals. That suggests quant noise pattern rather than pure detok bug. But detok mis-order could amplify it.

kenji: Agree. If quant noise moves neutrals across boundary, bidi transform might mirror them differently. Also investigating whether our tokenizer locale heuristics insert ZWSP at certain boundaries and if quantization causes model to prefer extra ZWSP token id.

priya: Action items: (1) kenji run kernel parity & q5k-shared (ETA 6h), (2) lucas produce top-20 token-id divergences with unicode classes (ETA 3h), (3) noah run small human QA batch for JP/KR (ETA EOD), (4) ops to hold q5k rollout on Dedicated until regression fix or fallback to q8 (noah).

noah: I'll hold canary until we see parity results. If q5k-shared reduces jitter we can consider a phased opt-in.

kenji: will update thread with parity logs and a short script that extracts kvcache traces for repeated sequence correlation.

lucas: sample helper to print bidi classes:```python
import unicodedata
def bidi_classes(s):
    return [(c, unicodedata.bidirectional(c)) for c in s]
```

priya: Thanks. Tagging @product and @support in case customers report recent spacey JP/KR outputs.

kenji: Ping me if you see any blocking examples in logs; attaching first two failing sample ids: `vela-q5k-431222-pt-001`, `vela-q5k-431222-pt-002`."
